subject.title: session.reset: support mode: "never" for manual-only session reset behavior

question: Which public `session.reset.mode` literal and validation semantics should OpenClaw support for manual-only reset behavior?
rationale: This adds a new public configuration value and affects session lifecycle semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent config contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add `never` mode
options.body: Adopt the reporter's literal, reject or ignore daily/idle-only fields in that mode, and document it as no automatic reset with manual `/new` and `/reset` still available.

options.title: Add `off` or `manual` mode
options.body: Support the same behavior but choose a different canonical literal that better matches existing OpenClaw config vocabulary.

options.title: Keep workaround only
options.body: Leave `daily | idle` as the only modes and document the large-idle workaround, accepting the readability and eventual-expiry tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Add `never` mode
recommendation.body: Adopt the reporter's literal, reject or ignore daily/idle-only fields in that mode, and document it as no automatic reset with manual `/new` and `/reset` still available.

likelyOwner.reason: The daily reset feature and current reset config lines trace most strongly to this history, making this the best available routing candidate for the product contract choice.
